newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council concludes land and air transport items.
newsitem.headline: Council concludes land and air transport items.

text.p: The Transport Council concluded a heavy agenda on Thursday with a compromise deal for renewed talks with Switzerland and agreement on a series of proposals for bus transport and air carrier liability.
Ministers also heard a report from Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock about talks on aviation relations between the United States and the EU in late October.

Kinnock said the next meeting was probably due next April in Brussels. He added at a post-Council news conference that U.S. officials had shown particular interest in talks related to computer reservation systems, code-sharing agreements and ownership control rules but showed reserves about competition questions.

Further work was required, Kinnock said, to convince Washington of the EU's good intentions in proposing a dispute settlement system which he said was not intended to be some sort of back door re-regulation.
Council also adopted a common position on proposal COM(96)190 to change Council Regulation 684/92 on common rules on the international carriage of passengers by coach and bus.

Ministers held an orientation debate on the Commission's proposal COM(94)323 for a Council regulation amending the Council directive and regulation on recording equipment in road transport (tachographs). They maintained the idea of two possible systems, an updated version of the existing system and a second, chip-based one, sending the file back to the Committee of Permanent Representations (COREPER).

Ministers also debated and adopted conclusions on the Commission's recommendation for a decision to allow it to begin talks aimed at getting Community membership of Eurocontrol, the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation. They also considered Commission's proposal, adopted on Wednesday, to join the Joint Aviation Authorities, asking COREPER to prepare the file for their March Council next year.
